facts.text: Dot Lake once served as a seasonal hunting camp linked by ancient Native freight trails to the Yukon River.
Doris Charles moved her family to Dot Lake in the mid‑1940s, turning abandoned camp structures into homes and forming a core of five Native families.
The Mansfield‑Ketchumstuk band of Upper Tanana Athabascans occupied the territory Dot Lake, stretching from the Fortymile River north to Tanana River and east to the Tok River mouth.
Dot Lake sits at 63°39′31″N 144°3′57″W, placing it deep within Alaska's interior.
The Native Village of Dot Lake hosts a Culture Camp July 6‑8, 2026, where participants learn traditions, language, and songs.
A July 17, 2026 news article highlights Dot Lake Village’s efforts to build safer, stronger communities through culture, public safety, and victim services.
